messages:
Maya Chen: FYI customer (BetaRetail) escalated — we're seeing p99 regressions on /v1/chat/completions. p95 steady ~330ms, p99 jumping to 1.8-2.5s sporadically. Started ~2026-03-15T14:22Z.
Samir Patel: copy. Any runtime error noise? OOMs, cuda errors, eviction churn?
Maya Chen: quick grep of runtime logs shows repeated allocation failures and large resident set on one GPU in cluster-prod-eu: 
```
[2026-03-15T14:24:11Z] WARN runtime: allocation failed: cudaMalloc returned out of memory
[2026-03-15T14:24:11Z] INFO runtime: attempt to evict KV cache -> freed 0 bytes (fragmented)
[2026-03-15T14:24:12Z] INFO runtime: request delayed, queue depth 9
```
Leo Kim: sounds like fragmentation + a tenant's KV blew up. Yesterday I saw similar when the per-tenant prefix cache didn't respect the max.
infra-bot: alert: runtime_gpu_memory_pressure=0.87 cluster=prod-eu shard=hawk-32g. p99 latency anomaly detected 2026-03-15T14:20Z -> 14:50Z.
Natalie Ruiz: propose quick mitigations:
• route-level rate-limit for BetaRetail to 30rps via console
• move their route to fallback-model redwood-lite-cpu for 15m
• enable kv.prefix_limit=2GB for that tenant (via feature flag)
Ryan O'Neill: +1. Also we can toggle allocator decay to force arenas to be returned: set MALLOC_CONF="arena_decay_ms:60000,retain_threshold:1" on a small canary set. That should help fragmentation.
Samir Patel: I'll run a triage checklist first: gather per-pod KV sizes, GPU memory histograms, and allocator stats. Commands: 
```bash
redwoodctl metrics query --name=runtime.kv.size --filter=tenant=BetaRetail --from=60m
kubectl -n prod-eu exec pod/rl-runtime-xyz -- nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,memory.total --format=csv
kubectl -n prod-eu logs pod/rl-runtime-xyz -c runtime | grep -i "arena\|jemalloc\|tcmalloc"
```
Maya Chen: metrics show one pod with kv.size ~29GB and resident GPU mem 27.5GB (total 32GB). Others 2-5GB.
Samir Patel: ok that's our smoking gun. Two immediate actions: throttle + force their traffic to the smaller model. I'll also deploy a canary with KV eviction adjusted: EVictThreshold=0.6 and enable incremental_kv_eviction=true.
Leo Kim: prefer rolling canary of 2 pods to validate MALLOC_CONF change and eviction flag. Avoid full redeploy to reduce risk.
Samir Patel: deploying canary now to two pods in prod-eu, targeting the problematic shard.
ops-oncall: standing by. I'll watch queues and OOM logs, and will be ready to manually cordon a node if it gets unstable.
infra-bot: canary created: rl-runtime-canary-2 pods. Initial GPU mem pressure on canary dropped to 0.45. p99 on canary-served requests ~420ms.
Maya Chen: customer reported partial improvement but still some spikes when large multi-turn requests hit.
Samir Patel: that's likely warmup and in-flight KV references. Next step: apply tenant-level KV cap to 2GB for BetaRetail and restart the offending pod after canary proves stable for 20m. Restart required to reclaim arenas in some cases (jemalloc holds arenas until process exits).
Ryan O'Neill: be careful: full restart creates momentary queueing. We should drain connections and do a graceful restart: 
```bash
kubectl -n prod-eu scale deployment/rl-runtime --replicas=0 --selector=pod=bad-pod --grace-period=60
# or use our drain helper
./infra/scripts/graceful-restart.sh pod/rl-runtime-bad --wait=120
```
Samir Patel: applying tenant cap flag now and scheduling a graceful restart in 30m. If canary stays healthy I'll roll eviction flags cluster-wide.
Natalie Ruiz: I'll update BetaRetail: telling them we applied temporary rate limit, moved to smaller model for stability, and will schedule a controlled pod restart. Asking them to hold off on heavy batch runs for next hour.
Samir Patel: follow-ups:
1) roll the eviction + MALLOC_CONF to remaining pods in shard after 30m of canary stability (staggered 10% increments).
2) postmortem: root cause likely bug in prefix_cache eviction (doesn't decrement refcount on multi-prefix hit) — causes unbounded KV growth for some tenants.
3) long-term: expose per-tenant KV caps, auto-fallback to CPU model on repeated cudaMalloc failures, and allocator telemetry in console.
Leo Kim: I'll own the postmortem and run experiments on jemalloc vs tcmalloc with our workload; may propose arena decay default changes.
ops-oncall: Canary looks stable. No OOMs in last 12m. Ready for roll.
Samir Patel: rolling to rest of prod-eu shard now (staggering). Will monitor p99 and GPU pressure.
infra-bot: rollout progress: 30% -> 60% -> 100% complete. Overall cluster GPU memory pressure down to 0.38. p99 endpoint latency back to ~470ms.
Maya Chen: closing loop with customer. They've acknowledged reduction and will watch for anomalies.
Natalie Ruiz: filing incident ticket INC-2026-042 with timeline, flags applied, and customer comms.
Samir Patel: after we stabilize, I'll create a small test that reproduces the prefix-evict leak so we can verify the patch.
Maya Chen: thanks all. Summary: root cause tenant-level KV leak + allocator arena retention -> fragmentation -> cudaMalloc failures -> p99 spikes. Temporary mitigations: rate-limit, smaller model, tenant KV cap, eviction tuning, allocator env on canary + rolling rollout. Owners: Samir (runtime fix & rollout), Leo (allocator experiments + postmortem), Natalie (customer comms), ops-oncall (watch).
